record.title: A preprint reports label-free visual grounding gains at inference, but not from pilot distillation
record.summary: A September 21, 2026 arXiv preprint evaluates a model's sensitivity to question-relevant image crops as a label-free visual-evidence signal. On one 191-example V*Bench evaluation using three Qwen vision-language models, the authors report that selecting among 16 candidate crops raised fine-grained answer accuracy from about 70% to 85% and localized target regions 4.4–5.1 times above chance. Combining the evidence-gap signal with model confidence improved correctness prediction in the reported test. The authors also tested gated self-distillation: on HR-Bench, no gating, trajectory gating and token gating all scored below the base model, with more aggressive gating performing worse. The inference and training findings come from different tests and should remain separate. Results are author-reported, unreproduced and limited to one small benchmark; the crop search also requires 16 forward passes per example.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The arXiv v1 preprint exists and defines a contrastive evidence-gap score based on how a model's token probabilities change between question-relevant and irrelevant image crops; it separately tests answer-peakedness to select a crop at inference.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across three Qwen vision-language models on one V*Bench evaluation, the authors report that selecting from 16 candidate crops localized answer regions 4.4–5.1 times above chance and raised direct-attribute answer accuracy from about 70% to about 85%. The result is author-reported, unreproduced and uses one 191-example benchmark.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that combining evidence-gap and model-confidence signals improved correctness prediction, with AUC up to 0.99, and that the evidence signal identified confidently wrong answers in a high-confidence subset. The results apply to the tested benchmark and split.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On an HR-Bench pilot training comparison using Qwen2.5-VL-7B with LoRA and 300 steps per arm, the authors report that ungated on-policy distillation and two gated variants all underperformed the base model; the per-token gate performed worst. This negative training result does not negate the separate inference-time crop-selection result.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent replication on V*Bench or a disjoint visual-grounding benchmark was found.

Reported region discovery requires a 16-crop grid/16 forward passes per example, but the paper does not compare against efficient crop-search and attention/Grad-CAM baselines across multiple datasets.
The selectivity plot is described in the source as an illustrative reconstruction whose underlying data should be used to replot it; detailed validation of that figure is missing.

brief.importance_rationale: If independently validated, a label-free measure of how much relevant image evidence changes a model's answer could improve inference-time visual search and confidence calibration without curated answer labels. The potential is meaningful for multimodal reliability, but current evidence is one unreproduced 191-example benchmark across three related Qwen models, requires 16 crop evaluations, and does not show pilot-scale training gains.
limitations: One unreproduced preprint and one 191-example V*Bench evaluation; models are three Qwen vision-language variants, not a broad family sample.
The crop-discovery method uses 16 candidate crops and therefore 16 forward passes per example; end-to-end latency and cost advantages were not established.
Reported accuracy uses multiple-choice answer letters at a fixed maximum image size; broader grounding metrics such as intersection-over-union and tests across additional datasets are needed.
The training-time negative result is a pilot with Qwen2.5-VL-7B, LoRA and 300 steps per arm; it does not establish that all evidence-gated training approaches fail.
The paper describes one selectivity curve as an illustrative reconstruction that should be replotted from the underlying data; it is not treated here as validated quantitative evidence.
brief.summary: A September 21, 2026 arXiv preprint evaluates a model's sensitivity to question-relevant image crops as a label-free visual-evidence signal. On one 191-example V*Bench evaluation using three Qwen vision-language models, the authors report that selecting among 16 candidate crops raised fine-grained answer accuracy from about 70% to 85% and localized target regions 4.4–5.1 times above chance. Combining the evidence-gap signal with model confidence improved correctness prediction in the reported test. The authors also tested gated self-distillation: on HR-Bench, no gating, trajectory gating and token gating all scored below the base model, with more aggressive gating performing worse. The inference and training findings come from different tests and should remain separate. Results are author-reported, unreproduced and limited to one small benchmark; the crop search also requires 16 forward passes per example.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report 4.4–5.1x above-chance localization and an increase from about 70% to 85% fine-grained accuracy using selected crops; combining evidence gap with confidence yielded correctness AUC up to 0.99. Pilot gated-distillation variants did not beat the base model.
technical.compute_or_cost: The reported selection over a 16-crop grid uses 16 forward passes per example. No end-to-end latency/cost comparison is established.
technical.demonstrated_result: The public preprint defines the signal and reports experiments. the research desk did not independently reproduce or verify the reported performance.
technical.implementation_status: Research method evaluated in a preprint; no independently audited implementation or deployment evidence was established.
technical.mechanism: Compare the model's answer-token likelihood under a question-relevant image crop and an irrelevant crop. For inference-time crop discovery, score candidate crops by answer-distribution peakedness and retain the selected crop; use the contrastive gap alongside confidence as a predictor of answer correctness. A separate training method uses the gap to weight on-policy self-distillation trajectories.
technical.novelty: Separates a crop-selection use of answer peakedness from a contrastive, per-token signal for evidence sensitivity, and tests the same general signal at inference time and in a pilot training objective.
technical.regime: Three models (Qwen2.5-VL-7B, Qwen3-VL-8B, Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B) evaluated on V*Bench n=191: direct_attributes n=115 and relative_position n=76. Input images are downsized to at most 1280 pixels; crop discovery uses a 16-crop grid. Training pilot uses Qwen2.5-VL-7B with LoRA for 300 steps per arm, evaluated on HR-Bench.
technical.reproducibility: Methods and tables are present in the arXiv HTML, but no independent replication or external benchmark evaluation was found. The authors say one selectivity plot is illustrative and should be replotted from underlying data.
technical.strongest_baseline: For crop selection, the authors compare full-image, center, random, anti-selected, peakedness-selected and oracle-box conditions. For training, the base model and ungated OPD are compared with trajectory- and token-gated variants.

brief.title: A preprint reports label-free visual grounding gains at inference, but not from pilot distillation
brief.why_it_matters: A cheap signal that identifies whether an answer changes when the relevant visual evidence is shown could help detect perception failures and guide inference-time crop selection without answer labels. The tested gains are preliminary and compute-bearing, and the paper's pilot training method did not improve over its base model.
